title: S3 Storage Classes & Lifecycle
summary: Match access patterns to S3 storage classes and automate transitions and expiration.
tldr: Pick the class from three facts in the question: **how often** data is read, **how fast** it must come back (milliseconds, hours, 12–48 h) and whether it must **survive an AZ loss**.
Known pattern → **Lifecycle rules** (Standard → IA/Glacier IR → Flexible → Deep Archive, then expire). Unknown or changing pattern → **Intelligent-Tiering** (no retrieval fees, automatic).
Lifecycle also removes waste: **NoncurrentVersionExpiration** for old versions and **AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload** for orphaned parts. **Storage Lens** shows where that waste is.

keyFacts.text: Minimum storage charge for Standard-IA and One Zone-IA / Glacier Instant Retrieval / Glacier Flexible Retrieval / Glacier Deep Archive. Deleting earlier still bills the minimum.
Minimum billable object size in Standard-IA, One Zone-IA and Glacier IR. Lifecycle skips transitioning objects under 128 KB by default.
Metadata overhead billed for each object in Glacier Flexible Retrieval and Deep Archive. Bundle millions of tiny objects into large archives first.
Glacier Flexible Retrieval restore times for Expedited, Standard and Bulk. Deep Archive: Standard within 12 h, Bulk within 48 h.
Intelligent-Tiering moves objects between frequent, infrequent (30 days) and Archive Instant (90 days) tiers automatically. Optional Archive and Deep Archive Access tiers need restores.

keywords.answer: S3 Batch Operations restore with Bulk tier

keywords.answer: S3 Express One Zone directory bucket

traps: One Zone-IA fails any requirement to survive the loss of an Availability Zone; use it only for data you can regenerate.
Transitioning millions of tiny objects to Glacier or Deep Archive can cost more than leaving them, because of per-object transition requests and 40 KB overhead.
Suspending versioning does not delete existing noncurrent versions; only a lifecycle expiration rule or explicit deletes do.
Intelligent-Tiering does not delete anything and does not clean up multipart parts or old versions.
Standard-IA looks cheap, but frequent reads add retrieval fees; for unpredictable access choose Intelligent-Tiering.
Expedited retrieval for a large bulk restore is the expensive choice; Bulk is cheapest when the deadline is days.

sections.heading: Reading a lifecycle question
sections.body:
Write the timeline from the question, then map each phase:

- **Days 0–30, frequent** → S3 Standard.
- **Rare but instant** → Glacier Instant Retrieval (quarterly) or Standard-IA (monthly).
- **Rare, hours OK** → Glacier Flexible Retrieval.
- **Almost never, 12–48 h OK** → Deep Archive.
- **End of retention** → an Expiration action.

Remember that a lifecycle rule can filter on prefix, tags or object size, so different data in one bucket can follow different paths.
